method: Visual inspection of actual final-PDF pages rendered by Poppler at110dpi, with enlarged crops made from those rendered pages for dense or identity-changing regions. No annotation or renderer edits were made.
render_command: pdftoppm -r 110 -png output/pdf/cassette-front-review-r11-changes.pdf tmp/r11-pdf/page; secondary direct render used -f52 -l52 into tmp/r11-pdf/secondary.

pages_viewed.observations: Three-column index, legend, counts, page numbers, and provenance footer are readable. The page lists only changed photos and explicitly says unchanged photos remain in the ledger.

Both deleted r10 ghosts D23 and D28 remain separately identifiable at the top image edge. Current tags 23[24]* through 30[32]* and the footer mapping distinguish the eight retained cassettes; no number is covered by another tag.
Dense stacks remain legible, including the lower group and tiny row57 fragment. Changed boxes and unchanged corners use the documented colors; footer blocks and page number fit.
All dense lower-stack row numbers are legible in the full page and enlarged crop, including rows25–33 and44–51. The restored right point on33 is visible; no overlapping tag rectangles are apparent.
Dense stack tags are readable. Row47 carries an amber held-box outline alongside magenta changed styling; the lower footer states the unresolved seam/instance question without truncation.

Added front48+ and retained front49[48] are separate, readable, and bound to distinct white fragments in the gripper aperture. No unavailable corner marker is drawn. Existing50[49] and the r10-to-current footer mapping remain readable.
Held row25 has a readable amber tag and box separate from unchanged cyan rows24/26. The footer explains why the requested positive x shift is held. All three footer columns and the page number fit.

acceptance.scope: Index plus six requested risk-bearing photo pages only.

limits: This is a bounded visual layout review, not a fresh annotation pass or a visual inspection claim for all55pages.
Programmatic all-page image hashes, decoded RGB equivalence, exact replay, navigation, and collision checks are recorded by the independent final readback/layout QA.
Dense native photo detail remains dependent on PDF zoom; the source photographs are not altered by these render inspections.
